title: Rami bar Abba (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Megillah 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.26b.3), while building a synagogue, he came before Rav Papa, who forbade it to him; before Rav Huna [son of Rav Yehoshua, as it should read], who answered him. Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim and Yuchasin read that he came before Rav Papi and R’ Huna bar Tachlifa. Hyman concludes that he was late according to all the readings.

It is possible that he was the father-in-law of Rav Ashi, as in [Chullin 111a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.111a.13): ‘Rav Ashi came to the house of Rami bar Abba, his father-in-law; he saw his son roasting liver,’ etc. Hyman says, ‘We have already explained in the entry on Rav Ashi that it should read Rami bar Chama.’ But it is possible to say that he [Rav Ashi] had two wives. So is the reading of the [She’iltot, Emor](https://www.sefaria.org/Sheiltot_d'Rav_Achai_Gaon.107.1) (cited by Hyman as 72), that Rami bar Abba was Rav Ashi’s father-in-law, from [Beitzah 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.29b.5); Hyman says, ‘Our reading there is Rami bar Chama.’ See the entry on R’ Ami bar Abba.[^1]

notes.text: [Dikdukei Soferim, Megillah 26b, note ס](https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/-jX67HTMEIwC?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=PA135) gives a manuscript line with Huna bar Tachlifa. [Sefer Yuchasin, London 1857, p. 128](https://www.daat.ac.il/daat/vl/yohasin-zakut/yohasin-zakut08.pdf#page=32) lists Huna bar Tachlifa, Papi and Rami together. The consulted Megillah has both sages forbid the action; [Hyman, vol. III, p. 1100](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=267) says Huna answered him. The liver episode continues on [Chullin 111b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.111b.1). Beitzah and the consulted She’iltot give different fathers for Ashi’s wife. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3243&lang=en) considers related textual and chronological difficulties.
